question:
B. Is this measure already running in City of Helsinki (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how much?
Measure: Nurse navigator for every suspected lung cancer. A named nurse books and chases every test, calls the patient, prepares the MDT and removes waiting between steps from referral to first treatment.
effect_summary_en: The scoping review abstract says patient navigation was consistently linked to faster first treatment, but it gives no pooled difference in days or percent against usual care.
supported_en: A 2026 scoping review of 13 studies (Japan Journal of Nursing Science) links cancer patient navigation with faster first treatment.
not_supported_en: No page shows the 15 % (0–30 %) shortening we assume, or any figure measured in lung cancer against usual care.
summary_en: HUS's lung cancer pathway page (dated 15.06.2026) says a doctor plans the further tests once the referral arrives and that patients meet a nurse at the first visit for guidance and advice. It does not describe a named nurse who books and chases every step, and searches found no HUS or Helsinki nurse coordinator, project or pilot, so there is no public sign of the measure. A 2026 scoping review of 13 studies says navigation was consistently associated with faster first treatment, but its abstract gives no size of effect.
unanswered_en: We found no HUS or City of Helsinki page about a lung cancer nurse coordinator, project or pilot, and no lung cancer effect size against usual care.
